title: Skill 04 · Git 工作流三件套 — Super Individual
title_en: Skill 04 · Git Workflow Skills — Super Individual

questions.question: 用 commit 类 skill 自动写提交信息，按文章，什么时候让它写效果最好？为什么？
options: 提交前先跑完全部测试，因为测试结果能告诉模型改动目的
刚改完、还在原会话里时，因为改动的动机此刻还在上下文中
攒满一周统一补写，因为模型能看到更完整的改动全貌
合并进主干之后再写，因为那时 diff 最终稳定不再变化
questions.explanation: 这类 skill 只吃 git diff，diff 完整回答「改了什么」却完全不含「为什么」。刚做完时 why 还在对话上下文里；隔天再补就只剩 diff，模型只能把 what 换个说法再讲一遍。文章明说「攒一周统一补」是最没用的用法。
questions.question_en: According to the article, when should you have a commit-message skill write the message, and why?
options_en: After running the full test suite, because the results tell the model what the change was for
Right after the change, in the same session, because the reason for it is still in context
After batching a week of work, because the model then sees a fuller picture of the changes
After merging to main, because the diff is final and no longer changing at that point
questions.explanation_en: These skills consume only the diff, which fully answers 'what changed' and says nothing about 'why'. Right after the work, the why is still in the conversation; a day later only the diff remains and the model just restates the what. The article calls batching a week of commits the least useful way to use them.

questions.question: 你想确保 agent 永远不会执行 git push --force。按文章，最可靠的做法是？
options: 装上 finishing-a-development-branch 让人来把关
在 SKILL.md 里反复强调并加粗写明「不要强推」
安装 git-pushing，让它统一走自带的推送脚本
在 PreToolUse 钩子里用模式匹配直接拦下这条命令
questions.explanation: skill 注入的是指令，模型可能不听、可能没被触发；钩子是代码，在事件上无条件执行，可以直接拒绝这次调用。有确定答案的交给钩子，需要判断的才交给 skill。脚本化推送和人工闸门各有用处，但都不是专门拦截这条命令的机制。
questions.question_en: You want to guarantee an agent never runs git push --force. According to the article, what is the most reliable approach?
options_en: Install finishing-a-development-branch so a human makes the call
Repeat 'never force-push' in bold, many times, in SKILL.md
Install git-pushing so every push goes through its bundled script
Block the command with a pattern match in a PreToolUse hook
questions.explanation_en: A skill injects instructions the model may ignore or never trigger; a hook is code that runs unconditionally on the event and can reject the call outright. Anything with a deterministic answer belongs in a hook; only judgment calls belong in a skill. Scripted pushes and human gates have their uses, but neither is a mechanism that specifically blocks this command.

questions.question: 按文章，Conventional Commits（feat: / fix: / BREAKING CHANGE）真正值钱的地方在哪里？
options: 替代代码审查，凡是格式合规的提交都可以免去人工的逐条检查
让 AI 写的提交信息也能准确地解释每次改动背后的动机和理由
提交时给下游机器留下结构化元数据，让版本号与 changelog 能被算出来
让提交历史在格式上整齐统一，方便团队成员在 review 时一眼快速浏览和查找
questions.explanation: 文章说 feat/fix/BREAKING CHANGE 不是格式洁癖，而是留给下游机器的元数据：diff → message → changelog 每往下一步都在丢信息，留了结构，changelog 和版本号才能算出来。格式整齐是附带的；它也补不了 diff 里缺的 why。
questions.question_en: According to the article, where does the real value of Conventional Commits (feat: / fix: / BREAKING CHANGE) lie?
options_en: It replaces code review, since any properly formatted commit can skip line-by-line human checks
It lets AI-written commit messages accurately explain the motivation behind each change
It leaves structured metadata for downstream tools, so version numbers and changelogs can be computed
It keeps commit history visually uniform so teammates can skim and search it quickly during review
questions.explanation_en: The article says these prefixes aren't formatting fussiness but metadata left for downstream machines: each step from diff to message to changelog loses information, and only with that structure can changelogs and versions be computed. Tidiness is a side effect, and the format can't supply the why that the diff lacks.
